title: E29 drop-back fires on representative-pipe death even when the bundle still has live members
detail: Packets traverse a pooled bundle edge (capacity = sum of members), but severance is detected via the single representative pipe. Killing the lowest-slot member resets all in-flight packets' progress; killing any other member does nothing.
recommended_fix: In the E29 pass, drop back only when the bundle has no live member left (or re-point Edge to a surviving member), preserving ProgressUnits across partial bundle loss.

title: Backward tick writes ReplayError through the E17 terminal freeze
detail: The backward-tick latch runs before the bTerminal check, so a post-terminal backward call mutates serialized state (ReplayError rides the T1 hash) despite the documented freeze.
recommended_fix: Move the bTerminal check above the backward-tick latch, or explicitly document ReplayError as exempt from the E17 freeze.

title: BuildProbeScenario doc comment stacked onto SpawnFixture; BuildProbeScenario itself undocumented
evidence:
+// BuildProbeScenario — construct the golden scenario's RUN SETUP: the
+// fixture (spawned nodes) + the logged draw commands + the demand plan.
+// The action log is populated with apply_tick=1 draws; the runner feeds the
+// log entries to Step at their tick (the replay path — the same one replay
+// uses, so the golden proves command application, not just the heartbeat).
+// SpawnFixture — the SHARED static fixture (UAD-17; r1 warning: PIE
+// hand-copied these positions): 1 source terminal, 1 router junction, 1
+// sink terminal at the golden scenario's grid positions. Run setup — never
+// in the action log (like the seed, re-created identically on every replay).
+inline void SpawnFixture(FSimState &State)
detail: Two function doc blocks are merged into one comment attached to SpawnFixture; BuildProbeScenario below has no doc of its own. Misleads anyone scanning the header by symbol.
recommended_fix: Split the stacked block: keep SpawnFixture's doc on SpawnFixture and move BuildProbeScenario's doc directly above its own definition.

title: Headers defer ECMP/bundles to stories 2.1/2.2 while this diff implements, wires, and tests them
evidence:
+// form: no BFS route cache, no LB, ever (ECMP is 2.2; bundles 2.1; QoS 3.x).
...
+// takes it mod N. (class is a forward parameter — slice 3 packet types; 2.2
+// passes 0 for every packet.)
...
+		const uint32_t Pick = EcmpPick(P.Src, P.Dst, static_cast<uint8_t>(P.Class), P.Id, Count);
detail: FlowStep already calls EcmpPick over multi-hop ECMP sets and passes P.Class, contradicting comments placing ECMP at 2.2 and class=0-until-2.2. The story references will mislead maintainers.
recommended_fix: Update the PP_Flow.h, PP_Routing.h, and PP_Bundles.h headers to state that ECMP and bundles are delivered in this slice.

title: Golden 'spawned' reported as delivered+live instead of the exact NextPacketId
detail: NextPacketId is serialized and exact (ids start at 1). The derived sum silently under-reports the moment any packet is culled without delivery (drop, timeout), corrupting the cross-runner golden contract.
recommended_fix: Print State.Flow.NextPacketId for flow_summary.spawned; remove the delivered+live derivation from the golden surface.

title: --probe-negative greps a relative log path while abslog writes an absolute one
detail: The script computes ROOT but never cds to it. Invoked from any cwd other than the repo root, both greps read a nonexistent file and the leg reports false failures.
recommended_fix: Set log="$ROOT/Saved/Logs/headless-probe-negative-${tag}.log" to match the abslog target exactly.

title: Bare same-tick re-step still double-spawns demand and redraws the nonce
evidence:
+	// WITH commands is a replay divergence (the commands were already applied
+	// at this tick); latch it. A bare same-tick re-step (no commands) is
+	// deliberately allowed — the step_once test convention re-steps tick 1.
+	if (Tick == State.Tick && NumCommands > 0)
detail: The guard only latches when commands are present. A bare re-step of a demand tick silently spawns duplicate packets and mutates the hash — the exact asymmetry the comment describes as the original defect.
recommended_fix: Latch or no-op all same-tick re-steps; give the step_once test convention an explicit re-step entry point instead.
